arithmetic: Exact rational arithmetic; Python Fraction/comb/factorial; no sympy.

ranges.root_cases: ordered Toeplitz x=0 plus universal proper rational functions, degrees2..8

scope: Closed coefficient formula agrees with independently reconstructed generating functions.
All coefficients of Euler ODE checked, including k=0 and k=d+1.
Terminating hypergeometric coefficients and parameter omission checked, including zero terminal term.
Left binomial formulas checked with p/q exchanged.
Right and left finite-root formulas agree with exact formal division at rational roots.
Confluent derivative coefficients checked through exact Taylor expansion, including mixed multiplicities and cancelled poles.
Actual binomial p=q=2 evaluated at x=625/36 with rational simple roots; scalar x=4 double root checked.
Highest differential coefficient after cancellation of x checked, and nonremovable finite singular points 0,c verified.
No floating-point root finding; mpmath unavailable in the selected runtime.

algebraic_derivation.ODE: For k>=1, D(k)c_k=R(k-1)c_(k-1). At k=0, D(0)=0 because j=q-b. At k=d+1, R(d)=0 because j=N-qd lies in {0,...,q-1}.
algebraic_derivation.hypergeometric: The factorial coefficient quotient gives p numerator parameters and q numerator parameters; the m denominator parameters include exactly one 1, at j=q-b. Removing it supplies k!, and the scaling is p^p*q^q/m^m=1/c.
algebraic_derivation.root_right: For simple nonzero roots, N/Q=sum_j N(z_j)/(Qprime(z_j)*(z-z_j)); expansion at z=0 gives the minus sign and z_j^(-n-1).
algebraic_derivation.root_left: Qvee(w)=w^m Q(1/w), hence (Qvee)prime(1/z_j)=-z_j^(2-m)Qprime(z_j). Substitution in the right residue formula gives the positive sign and z_j^(n+m-1).
algebraic_derivation.classical: At p=q=b=1 the Euler operator is x times [x(4-x)ypp+(6-3x)yp+n(n+2)y]. Polynomial identity permits canceling x.
algebraic_derivation.confluent: gamma_(j,r) is the coefficient of w^(mu_j-r) in N(rho_j+w)/D_j(rho_j+w), namely the stated derivative divided by factorial.
algebraic_derivation.singularities: After division by x, highest coefficient is p^p q^q x^(m-1)(c-x). First-derivative coefficient at0 is D(1)>0; derivative-(m-1) coefficient atc is c^(m-2)m^m(1/2-m), nonzero. Thus neither top-coefficient zero is a removable common scalar factor.

assumptions: Hypergeometric formula is stated for n>=b-1 (left: n>=a-1); earlier components vanish.
Finite-root formulas require all m roots of Q simple; omega and the extreme coefficient are nonzero, hence no root is zero.
Repeated roots are handled by the derivative/principal-part formula, as independently checked.
